extracted.intended_audience: statesmen, political reformers, and readers of political theory interested in designing stable republican constitutions
extracted.subtask_description: A prescriptive plan for structuring a durable republic (commonwealth) that balances social orders, prevents concentration of power, and provides institutional checks, representation, rotation, and judicial accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three orders must be gratified
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three orders of men in every state, and for that reason there should also be three ranks or degrees in a republic, and no more; those who model a commonwealth must take such provisions as may gratify three sorts of men, of which all states are composed, that is, the high, the middle sort, and the low.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to satisfy the humours and inclinations of all three classes will naturally end in ruin; it is absolutely necessary to gratify the ambition of all three ranks so each sees its proper share in the administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sovereignty lodged in citizens; necessity of three powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The sovereign power is lodged, both of right and in fact, in the citizens themselves. Machiavelli perceived the necessity of three powers; but he did not see an equal necessity for the separation of the executive power from the legislative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design must recognize three powers for balance, though strict separation (e.g., executive vs. legislative) may be unnecessary in his view; concentrate on functional distribution rather than rigid separation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overly large or numerous councils (no council of a thousand)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appointment of officers in the council of a thousand would have ruined all the good effects of the other divisions of power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large, multiplicious councils create corruption, underhand practices, and faction; avoid creating many councils merely to make friends or dependants—only bodies conducive to good order should exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit tenure and prevent prolonged power concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: Defects of previous forms included that power was continued too long in the same persons; the elections were subject to fraud and underhand practices; there was no check upon the grandees to deter them from forming parties and factions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should prevent long continuance of power in the same hands, introduce checks on elites, limit opportunities for electoral fraud, and provide mechanisms to deter factional formation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure popular share in government
rubrics_metrics.description: The people had no share at all in the government. Without satisfying the common people, no republic ever yet stood upon a stable foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the lower rank an explicit and effective role (e.g., councils nominating magistrates) so the common people feel secure and invested in the system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid intermediate hybrid forms—choose a true principality or commonwealth
rubrics_metrics.description: No form of government can be devised that will be firm and lasting, which is not either a true principality, or a true commonwealth. All intermediate forms between these two extremes will be defective; they may be ruined two ways and thus are unstable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design should avoid half-measures and hybrid structures that leave the state vulnerable to collapse into either extreme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a dignified elder body (sixty-five) to restore authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Elect sixty-five citizens, of not less than forty-five years of age, to give dignity to the government; fifty-three out of the highest class and twelve out of the next; they should continue in the administration for life, subject to certain restrictions: one of them to be appointed standard-bearer of justice for two or three years (or for life).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An elder, dignified senate-sized body lends gravitas; life tenure combined with specific restrictions and rotating major offices preserves dignity while allowing controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divide ruling elites into alternating bodies (two 32-member divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The other sixty-four citizens already elected should be divided into two distinct bodies, each consisting of thirty-two; one division, in conjunction with the standard-bearer, should govern the first year and the other the next, so they are changed alternately every year and all together should be called the signori.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternating governance and smaller rotating groups prevent domination by any single cohort and ensure regular turnover of executive functions among elites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Further subdivide for rotation and residence to handle day-to-day business
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the thirty-two be divided into four parts of eight each; every one of which should reside three months in its turn with the standard-bearer in the palace, assume the magistracy with the usual forms and ceremonies, and transact all business formerly handled by larger councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short residential rotations concentrate responsibility while limiting continuous control; expands experienced membership available for embassies and other functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a council of two hundred (council elect) with middle-class dominance
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint a council of two hundred, every member not less than forty years of age; one hundred and sixty taken out of the middle class, and the other forty out of the lower, to continue for life and be called the council elect; this council, in conjunction with the sixty-five, should transact the affairs previously managed by abolished councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a stable governing chamber representing the middle class strongly; appointments may be vested in a higher authority for initial support (in text, by 'your holiness').

rubrics_metrics.name: Revive a popular nominating council (council of a thousand or six hundred)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revive the council of a thousand, or at least one of six hundred citizens, who should nominate all the magistrates and officers in the manner they used to do formerly, except the sixty-five, the council of two hundred, the eight di guardia, and the balia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retaining a larger popular nominating body satisfies the common people and provides legitimacy for magistrate selection while excluding certain elite institutions from its nominations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize militia into distinct corps with appointed commissioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Divide the militia into distinct corps, over which you may appoint two commissioners, one for each; by these provisions two out of the three classes may be thoroughly satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Split military command among separate commissioners to distribute influence and prevent military monopoly by any faction or class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institute local standard-bearers, gonfaloniers, and short-term prevots by lot
rubrics_metrics.description: Appoint sixteen standard-bearers over the companies of the citizens; increase the number of divis, assistants to the gonfalonier and commanding detachments; after appointment, draw four prevots out of them by lot to continue in office one month, so that at the end of four months they will all have been prevots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sortition and short terms to broaden participation, reduce entrenchment, and spread authority across the citizenry, while ensuring oversight of magistrates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place resident inspectors with limited veto ('put a stop') on council acts
rubrics_metrics.description: A resident officer should be present with the resident signori; without the presence of this officer, the resident signori should not be allowed to pass any act, nor should he himself have any vote there, but only be a witness and inspector of their proceedings, to which he may be suffered to put a stop till he has asked the opinion of all the thirty-two together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed oversight officers who can temporarily halt actions (but not decide) and require broader consultation before resolutions proceed; creates a check without concentrating decision power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require quorum and cross-institutional checks for resolutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Even the thirty-two, when all together, should not have power to resolve upon any thing, except two of the said prevots were present, who should have no further authority than to put a stop to their resolutions for a time, and report them to the council elect; nor should that council have power to resolve upon anything, except that at least of the sixteen gonfaloniers and two prevots were there who should only have the liberty of taking the matter out of the hands of that council and referring it to the great council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design decision rules requiring presence of specific officers and permitting referral to higher popular councils; prevents unilateral enactment by single bodies and preserves right of appeal and broader deliberation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish a criminal court with lot-chosen members and face-to-face proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a court consisting of the eight di guardia and a balia of thirty citizens, to be chosen by lot out of the council of two hundred and that of six hundred together; this court should have power in criminal cases of summoning the accuser and accused to appear face to face before it in a certain time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a court is of great use where citizens are afraid to call great and powerful delinquents to account; lot-selection and ballots enable free and secure judgment—many must concur to accuse so that judgments (often by ballot) can be given safely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design constitution to prevent violent usurpation by satisfying ambitions and clarifying spheres
rubrics_metrics.description: The only way to prevent the evils (sudden heads rescuing the state by violence or one part opening the council of a thousand and sacrificing the other) is to establish the several classes and ordinances of the commonwealth in such a manner that they may support themselves; when each rank has its due share in the administration, knows his proper sphere of action, and whom he can confide in; and lastly, when no one has any occasion to wish for a change of government either because his ambition is not gratified, or that he does not think himself sufficiently secure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, self-sustaining institutional roles, equitable shares of power, and perceived security for each class reduce incentives for insurrection, executions, banishments, and confiscations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use honors and voluntary distinction to attract public service
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest honour that can be attained by any man is that which is voluntarily conferred on him by his countrymen; the greatest good he can do ... is that which he does to his country. Those who have reformed kingdoms and commonwealths by wholesome laws and constitutions have been highly coveted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide avenues for voluntary honour and public glory (e.g., constitutional reform, public office) as incentives for capable and ambitious men to work for the public good rather than private domination.
